details: CONFIRMED (reproduced with the hook). sync_merge accepts the literal word FETCH_HEAD without asking what it holds.
FETCH_HEAD is whatever the last `git fetch` wrote: any remote, any URL, or `.` (a local branch). `git fetch` is not in
GIT_WRITE, so the fetch half is allowed in main too. The guard runs before the command, so in the usual one-line form
`git fetch X && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD` it cannot even read the FETCH_HEAD that the merge will use; checking
its content at hook time sees the old value. So no fix inside "allow FETCH_HEAD, origin only" is exact unless the
guard parses the preceding fetch in the same command and also checks the current FETCH_HEAD when there is none.
Design: the brief asks for both "allow --ff-only FETCH_HEAD" and "origin is the only remote allowed (do not widen to
any remote)"; FETCH_HEAD is a widening to every remote. The design's own measurement (design-arsenal.md 1.2) names only
`git merge --ff-only origin/master` as arsenal's Master Sync; nothing measured needs FETCH_HEAD.
Recommendation: drop FETCH_HEAD (allow origin/<default> only). Size: 10 min (drop it, flip two test lines).
Keeping it with a parse of the preceding `git fetch origin [<default>]` plus a FETCH_HEAD==refs/remotes/origin/<default>
check when no fetch precedes: about 45 min and more parts (principle 7).
evidence: $ for c in ...; do printf '{...cwd: repro/g on master...}' | env -u CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR plugins/core/hooks/guard-main.sh; echo "$? :: $c"; done
0 :: git fetch . side && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD
0 :: git fetch https://example.invalid/x.git topic && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD
plugins/core/hooks/merge.py:282  for directory, branch in kit_guard.allowed_merges(command, cwd):   (wt/ names only)
failing_case: A main checkout on master (any repo; in a project with .relay/ the same holds). guard-main.sh fed
{"tool_name":"Bash","cwd":<main>,"tool_input":{"command":"git fetch . side && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD"}}
exits 0 (allowed), while "git merge --ff-only side" exits 2. Likewise
"git fetch https://example.invalid/x.git topic && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD" exits 0.
In relay itself, "git fetch . wt/unchecked && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD" is allowed by guard-main and
never seen by merge.py (allowed_merges lists only wt/ names), so a branch lands on master with no gate and no check mark.
Should: be refused, because the brief says origin is the only remote allowed and the merge hook lets a branch in
only with a green gate and open 0.
fix_hint: Return pos[0] == "origin/" + default; drop FETCH_HEAD from sync_merge, its docstring, the comment in git_write, the
guard-main.test.sh "ff-only FETCH_HEAD sync" line (make it a block case) and the test_merge_hook assertion (expect 2).
pass_cases: 1. main on master, "git merge --ff-only origin/master": allowed (exit 0), as now.
2. main on master, "git fetch . side && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD": refused (exit 2).
3. main on master, "git fetch https://example.invalid/x.git topic && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD": refused (exit 2).
4. main on master, "git merge --ff-only upstream/master" and "git merge --ff-only some-branch": refused (exit 2), as now.
5. If the owner keeps FETCH_HEAD: main on master, "git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD" and
"git fetch origin master && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD": allowed.
reason: tests/test_merge_hook.py:92 test_f1_fetch_head_is_not_a_sync passes; fails at 23dd17f. Shell cases in guard-main.test.sh block FETCH_HEAD and fetch-dot; origin/master still allowed (line 82 test).
findings.summary: FETCH_HEAD lets a main checkout fast-forward to any branch of any remote, URL or local branch: the origin-only rule and the merge gate are bypassed

details: CONFIRMED (reproduced). The regex r"\.claude/hooks/([\w.-]+)" matches any path that ends in .claude/hooks/<name>,
then checks only <root>/.claude/hooks/<name>. So a hook in the home folder, or any other path with that tail, is
judged "gone". And the rule runs in merge_settings, i.e. on every `relay setup`, not only after migrate moved
something: it deletes the owner's settings by file absence, not by what relay moved. Cause, not symptom (principle 6):
the cause of Q1 is that migrate forgets the entries of the files it moves; the fix belongs with the moved list, not
with a generic existence test. The setup message "removed a hook the plugins now provide" is also wrong for these.
Size: 20 min.
failing_case: Project .claude/settings.json with {"hooks":{"Stop":[{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"}]}],
"Notification":[{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"/Users/someone/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"}]}]}}, no
<root>/.claude/hooks/notify.sh. relay_setup.merge_settings(root, []) (run by every `relay setup`, not only migrate)
removes both entries and reports them as "removed a hook the plugins now provide". Should: keep both; relay did not
move them and does not provide them.
fix_hint: Pass the paths migrate moved (moved list, e.g. ".claude/hooks/issue-stage.sh") from migrate into setup/merge_settings
and drop only commands that name exactly those project paths ("$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/<path>, ./<path>, <path>);
pass_cases: 1. migrate(apply=True) on a project whose settings name "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/issue-stage.sh (moved aside)
and .../guard.sh (kept): issue-stage.sh entry gone, guard.sh entry kept (the existing test).
2. merge_settings / setup on a project whose settings name "~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh": entry kept.
3. Same with an absolute "/Users/someone/.claude/hooks/notify.sh": entry kept.
4. setup (no migrate) on a project whose settings name "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/later.sh that does not exist
and was never moved by relay: entry kept (relay does not delete what it did not move).
reason: tests/test_setup.py:273 passes, fails at 23dd17f; only migrate-moved paths are dropped (names_moved_hook).
